correctness.rationale: The signed weighted matrix tree identity gives W_n(S)=n^{-1} product_{i>=2}(n-2 lambda_i(L_H)). For any k-edge graph the largest Laplacian eigenvalue is <=k+1 by component sizes and the complementary Laplacian. Equality at k+1 forces one k-edge tree component whose complement is disconnected, uniquely a star. Therefore for n=2p signs are strictly positive below p-1 and nonnegative at p-1, with zero only for a p-vertex star. Odd n nonvanishing follows from Cayley parity. Exact independent checkers verify n=3..10 at the stated finite boundaries.

value.rationale: The first edge-parity frequency that can erase the spanning-tree signal is a natural stability/observability boundary, independent of minimum surviving multiplier magnitude. The theorem gives an all-n sharp cutoff, a complete extremizer classification and exact counts of first-frequency obstructions, not an arbitrary finite sample or standard isolated computation. It creates a structural boundary for more detailed tree Fourier nullity and constrained-edge measurement questions.
